What two fields are you actually studying?

Criminal Justice (with a focus on Criminology) and Philosophy.

Edit: I was in a hurry when making my post, but now I can elaborate what and why I'm studying:

Criminal Justice is my major, the only crime-related major offered at my local university. If I had a choice, I might have gone with forensics; forensics was my favorite subject during my final year of high school and was ultimately what pushed me into taking up crime studies. Nevertheless, CJ is still yet an exciting major to study; I get to learn everything from psychology and sociology of crime as well as serial killers, police history, and trial procedure.

As I stated previously, my focus within my major is Criminology. I took a course, fell in love with it, and now apply myself to all sorts of electives that deal with scientific analysis and motivations. I think this is truly what I've always wanted to know, not what police have done or how to catch a criminal, but why people turn to criminalization. Criminals are just everyday people except, you know, they committed crimes. Any one of us could be criminal. Any of us.

Philosophy is just something that I sort of stumbled upon. I always thought it was people who lounged around thinking about how to do everything the best way possible, sorta zen-ish. When just by curiosity I downloaded Philosophize This! podcast, it turns out that it is much deeper than that. What really turned me on was that one of the first discussions was about Socrates and Plato in which Socrates (as Plato's character) discusses what exactly is "justice" and how nobody can seem to give a straight definition. That immediate connection to my crime studies and the fact that philosophers have been debating about crime for thousands of years made me see just how worthwhile a study that philosophy is.

tl;dr: I like to study good and evil. Mostly evil.
